- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 75% of 30d mean, model often overestimates; apply downward bias of 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment cycle midpoint.
